findings.title: Operator feature requirement is stated unconditionally but default update behavior does not enable it
findings.body: The caution says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, with no qualification. However, `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` only enables the feature when an explicit `UpdateStrategy` is configured; the default/null strategy test cases exercise operator update behavior without it and are expected to succeed. This either overstates the requirement and will lead users to enable a preview feature unnecessarily, or the tests are not covering a real failure in the default path.

findings.title: Feature-disabled exit code and check subcommand are not tested
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises the `metadata` subcommand and asserts the error text, but does not assert the newly documented exit code 4 for the feature-disabled case. The `check` subcommand has an identical feature gate that is not covered in this test. A regression in the exit code or in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`'s feature gate would not be caught.

findings.title: Recreate exit code is not asserted
findings.body: The wrong-version tests assert the printed error messages but never assert that the command exits with `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` (now 3). The exit code is the documented contract for automation, and its value was changed in this PR, so the tests should verify it rather than relying only on output text.

findings.title: Public exit code meaning changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means the `rolling-updates` feature is disabled. This is a user-visible contract change for any scripts already written against the previous preview behavior, especially because the accompanying documentation tells users to rely on the exit code. If backward compatibility matters for preview users, this should be called out or a non-conflicting new code should be used.
